content.text: A collection website, a digital edition, a research application: Triiiceratops fits into the tools you already use.

attrs.note: The same viewer, with an integration suited to your framework.

attrs.label: Web component
attrs.note: Add a script and a viewer tag to an HTML page. No build step required—a straightforward fit for static sites, CMS templates, and server-rendered pages.

attrs.label: React
attrs.note: Import a typed component, pass props, and connect your application through React hooks.

attrs.label: Vue
attrs.note: Use a component and composables that bring viewer state into Vue’s reactivity.

attrs.label: Svelte
attrs.note: Import the Svelte component directly and work with it alongside the rest of your application.

content.text: Customize it easily with our configuration editor

Use the builder to try your own manifest, arrange the controls and panels, and choose a theme. See each change in a live viewer, then copy the code for your framework. You can also share a configuration for someone else to try.
Start simple. Connect more when you need it.

Embed a viewer on its own, or connect it to the rest of your application. Viewer state lets your interface follow navigation and drive the viewer; optional plugins add capabilities such as audio and video playback or image and PDF downloads.
The guides cover installation and integration. The builder is the quickest place to find the configuration you want.

meta.title: Fits the site you already have
meta.intro: Add Triiiceratops to an HTML page or import it through your bundler as a React, Vue, or Svelte component. Start with a IIIF manifest, then make the viewer your own.
